message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order placed and filled.**

I researched Apple's fiscal 2024 results (year ended September 28, 2024) and confirmed them against two independent primary sources. Apple's newsroom release reported quarterly revenue of $94.9B for Q4, up 6% YoY, and for the full fiscal year **total net sales of $391.0 billion** (net income $93.7B, or $6.08 per diluted share, including a one-time $10.2B tax charge). Apple's Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR corroborated this exactly: total net sales of $391,035 million (up from $383,285M in FY2023), net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08, and operating income $123,216M — showing modest revenue growth despite the tax hit, with a still-enormous operating margin and cash generation. The quote was $222.70 last (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.80 — essentially at market, ~0.04% above the ask — which filled at $222.80 for a total of roughly **$9,803**, comfortably inside every mandate constraint: AAPL only, buy side, under the $10,000 per-order cap, well under the $20,000 daily total, and no funds moved out of the account (cash was $50,000 with 100 MSFT shares held). I cited FY2024 total net sales of $391,035M plus supporting net income ($93,736M) and diluted EPS ($6.08) in the order's key figures.

Summary.
